newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends touch higher, holding new levels.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends touch higher, holding new levels.

text.p: COMEX copper settled slightly higher as the market paused for the second day running after the heady gains of the past week.
Traders were waiting for Friday's LME stock report though no major hike or dip was expected.

"I think we are moving through a transitional period - prices are much higher than they were, but it will be interesting to see demand at these higher price levels," said David Rinehimer of Smith Barney.
With the much stronger LME cash to three months backwardation, traders are watching closely to see if any surplus metal is lured back into LME warehouses.
The backwardation was at $134 to $144 on Thursday.
LME stocks have fallen dramatically since September, now down to six-year lows.
"It's hard to imagine all this stock draw down reflected a resurgence in consumption," Rinehimer said.
December COMEX settled 0.30 cent firmer at 105.85 cents, traded 106.30 to 104.75 cents.
Volume was estimated at 9,000 lots, much lower than the heavy trading of recent sessions. Official volume on Wednesday was 18,254 lots.
